stories.headline: Predictive functions move model judgment into SQL
stories.read_scope: Complete launch article: five beta SQL functions, dashboard and Genie surfaces, taxi-data examples, holiday and covariate support, fev-bench comparison and publisher-controlled quality claims.
stories.summary: Databricks introduced beta SQL functions for forecasting, driver analysis, anomaly detection, regression and classification, with results usable in queries, dashboards and Genie. Its examples show holidays and business covariates informing forecasts. Accuracy comparisons use a named benchmark, but the platform maintains the models and reports the results, so teams still need local baselines and error review.
stories.why_it_matters: Give analysts one governed dataset and prediction question, then compare the built-in function with an approved baseline across backtests, missing data and business shocks. Require visible inputs, uncertainty, refresh rules and an escalation path before decisions depend on results.
stories.image_alt_intent: An analyst sends governed SQL data into five predictive functions, then compares forecast, anomaly and driver outputs against a baseline and uncertainty review before dashboard use.

stories.headline: An AI business record needs its origin trail
stories.read_scope: Complete attorney analysis: AI records as ESI, Rule 37(e), prompts and source versions, model and system instructions, human revisions, legal holds, vendor retention, reconstruction limits and proportional preservation.
stories.summary: Reuters Legal commentary argues that consequential AI-generated business records may require more than the final document. Prompts, retrieved source versions, model identifiers, system instructions, intermediate outputs, human edits, approvals and triggered actions can determine whether a record is explainable or defensible. The author recommends proportional preservation, updated legal holds and vendor checks rather than retaining every interaction indefinitely.
stories.why_it_matters: Classify AI uses by consequence, then preserve the minimum origin package for high-risk records: inputs, versions, outputs, edits, approvals and actions. Test whether vendors can export that package before procurement, because rerunning a prompt cannot reconstruct historical context reliably.
stories.image_alt_intent: A consequential AI report links backward to versioned prompts, sources, model settings and system rules, then forward to human edits, approvals and automated actions in an auditable chain.
